name: Dusty Green
lede: Dusty Green is a mid green softened with grey, a plain descriptive name that appears in several color standards without a story of its own.

sections.title: A descriptive name
sections.body:
*Dusty green* is a description rather than an invention: a green with a little grey in it. Our library finds the name in the ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955, in Ridgway's standards of 1912, in Maerz and Paul's dictionary of 1930 and in the xkcd color survey of 2010 [1]. No coiner is documented in our sources [1].

Measured against the ISCC-NBS categories, the swatch lands nearest to moderate yellowish green, 7.5 units of ΔE2000 away [1]. Its closest relatives by name are [[sage-green]], [[moss-green]] and [[dusty-sage]].

sections.title: In the books
sections.body: The books use the words as plain description, not as a color name. St Clair describes the small leaves of the indigo shrub *Indigofera tinctoria* as slightly dusty green [2]. The dye plant is green and its prized colorant is blue, which is a useful reminder that a dye is made, not seen, in the leaf [2]. See [[indigo]] for the blue.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive this green appears in 15 paintings, 0.06 per cent of the total, as photographed [3]. Gustav Klimt accounts for 4 of the 15, from 50 of his paintings in the archive [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a color match is not a pigment test [3].

origin.first_recorded: undocumented; in Ridgway 1912 and Maerz and Paul 1930 per our library

field.dataset: ColorHub archive of about 23,800 paintings, as photographed

questions.q: Which does the word "dusty" tell you about this green?
True or false: the indigo plant's leaves are blue.

openers: A green with some grey in it is called dusty, and the leaves of the indigo plant are exactly that, not blue.
